title: Scaling Up Memory Disaggregated Applications with SMART
problem: IOPS-bound memory disaggregated applications are limited by network bandwidth when performing concurrent fine-grained remote memory accesses, failing to scale beyond 32 cores.
motivation: Memory disaggregation with RDMA is becoming prevalent, but network scalability bottlenecks prevent applications from fully utilizing modern many-core processors.
method: SMART optimizes remote memory access patterns through request batching, intelligent pipelining, and network-aware scheduling to improve IOPS throughput and enable scaling across many cores.
key_novelty: A system design that overcomes network IOPS bottlenecks to enable disaggregated memory applications to scale efficiently on many-core systems.
contributions: Identifies and quantifies the network IOPS bottleneck in disaggregated memory systems
Proposes SMART architecture for improved concurrent remote access handling
Achieves scaling beyond 32-core limitation on many-core machines
Provides architectural insights for disaggregated memory system design
limitations: Not discussed in the provided abstract.
